articleBlocks: I first thought the puzzle might be about sets of ten because some common groupings come in tens.
But then I considered the clue about bits in a byte, which clearly refers to a group of eight.
The clue about planets in our solar system also pointed towards eight, given the historical classification of our solar system.
However, it was the clue about the corners of a cube that made the pattern of eights undeniable, as a cube by definition has eight corners.
This realization made me reconsider my initial guess of sets of ten and look more closely at the pattern of eights across the clues.
Upon further reflection, the clue about legs on a spider also fits neatly into this pattern, as spiders are known for their eight legs.
Similarly, the clue about the sides of most stop signs, which are octagons, also references eight sides.
The turning point for me was recognizing how each of these clues, despite coming from different areas, all referenced the number eight.
In hindsight, the puzzle's answer, 'Things that come in eights,' is a clever play on the common thread among the clues.
This puzzle taught me to look for consistent patterns across seemingly unrelated clues.
The solution emerges clearly once you recognize the thread of eights throughout the clues.
